name: Circular Wait Implies Deadlock with Multi-Unit Resources
description: Believing a cycle in a Resource Allocation Graph (RAG) always guarantees deadlock, ignoring available multiple instances.
correction: A cycle is a necessary condition for deadlock only with single-instance resource types. With multi-instance resources, a cycle may not be a deadlock if other processes release instances.

name: Confusing Deadlock Prevention with Avoidance
description: Assuming Banker's Algorithm prevents deadlock by eliminating one of the 4 Coffman conditions, rather than dynamically assessing safe states.
correction: Deadlock prevention statically invalidates at least one Coffman condition; deadlock avoidance (like Banker's algorithm) allows all 4 conditions but dynamically rejects unsafe state transitions.

name: Atomic Instruction Sufficiency for Critical Section
description: Thinking a single atomic variable increment solves race conditions across multi-step transactions.
correction: Atomic single-variable operations only protect individual updates. Multi-step read-modify-write workflows still require transactional mutual exclusion or locks.

name: Virtual Memory Equals Swap Space
description: Assuming virtual memory is just disk paging/swap space rather than an abstraction providing private linear address spaces.
correction: Virtual memory is a memory management technique providing each process an isolated address space mapped to physical RAM via page tables; swap space is merely an overflow backing store.

name: Preemptive Scheduling Eliminates Starvation
description: Believing preemptive priority scheduling prevents low-priority processes from starving.
correction: Priority scheduling with preemption can cause severe starvation for lower priority tasks unless aging techniques are explicitly applied.

name: Safe State Equals Deadlock-Free Execution Guarantee
description: Believing that entering an unsafe state guarantees an immediate deadlock.
correction: An unsafe state is not a deadlock; it is merely a state from which the OS cannot guarantee all processes will finish if all request their maximum claims simultaneously.

name: Adding Indexes Always Accelerates Queries Without Tradeoffs
description: Believing secondary indexes improve all operations, ignoring write amplification and maintenance overhead.
correction: Every additional index requires synchronous updates on INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations, slowing write throughput and consuming memory buffers.

name: Composite Index Column Order Irrelevance
description: Thinking an index on (A, B, C) can efficiently satisfy a query filtering exclusively on WHERE B = 5.
correction: B-Tree composite indexes follow the leftmost prefix rule. A query filtering only on 'B' cannot utilize the (A, B) index hierarchically without scanning or index skip scans.

name: READ COMMITTED Prevents Non-Repeatable Reads
description: Assuming READ COMMITTED isolation level guarantees the same SELECT query in a transaction yields identical rows.
correction: READ COMMITTED prevents dirty reads, but another transaction can commit changes between two reads, causing non-repeatable reads. REPEATABLE READ is required.

name: Higher Normal Form Always Equals Higher Performance
description: Believing BCNF/3NF always outperforms 2NF or denormalized schemas in production read workloads.
correction: Higher normal forms minimize redundancy and update anomalies, but introduce heavy JOIN overhead for complex analytical read queries.

name: Clustered Index Copies Data Rows
description: Thinking a table can have multiple clustered indexes that duplicate the entire row store.
correction: The clustered index IS the physical ordering of the data rows in the leaf pages. Therefore, a table can only have one clustered index.

name: Atomicity Means Thread-Safe Concurrency
description: Confusing Atomicity (all-or-nothing completion) with Isolation (concurrency protection).
correction: Atomicity guarantees state rollbacks upon failure; Isolation guarantees concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other.

name: TCP Fast Retransmit Relies on Timeout Expiration
description: Believing TCP must wait for the Retransmission Timeout (RTO) before retransmitting a lost packet.
correction: Fast Retransmit triggers immediately upon receiving 3 duplicate ACKs without waiting for the timer-based RTO to expire.

name: UDP Lacks Reliability Because It Corrupts Packets
description: Thinking UDP does not perform checksums and delivers corrupt bitstreams.
correction: UDP has an optional/mandatory checksum to detect and discard corrupted packets; it simply does not provide ACKs, retransmissions, or ordering.

name: Flow Control and Congestion Control Are the Same
description: Treating receiver buffer management (Flow Control) as network bottleneck management (Congestion Control).
correction: Flow control protects the destination receiver's buffer (rwnd), while congestion control protects the intermediate network routers (cwnd).

name: HTTP/2 Completely Solves Head-of-Line Blocking
description: Believing HTTP/2 stream multiplexing eliminates packet loss Head-of-Line blocking at the TCP layer.
correction: HTTP/2 multiplexes streams over a single TCP connection; if one TCP packet is dropped, ALL multiplexed streams are blocked at TCP layer. HTTP/3 (QUIC/UDP) solves this.

name: Distance Vector Protocols Have Global Topology Maps
description: Assuming RIP/Distance-Vector algorithms know the full global network topology like OSPF (Link State).
correction: Distance Vector protocols only know vector distance and next-hop direction ('routing by rumor'), whereas Link State protocols construct the full topology graph.

name: Hash Table Lookups Are Unconditionally O(1)
description: Ignoring worst-case collision degradation to O(n) under pathological hash distributions or HashDoS attacks.
correction: Hash table operations are O(1) average case, but degrade to O(N) when all keys hash to the same bucket (or O(log N) with red-black tree buckets).

name: Binary Search Tree Always Guarantees O(log n) Operations
description: Forgetting that un-balanced BSTs degenerate into linked lists of depth O(n) on sorted insertions.
correction: A regular BST requires explicit self-balancing (AVL, Red-Black) to guarantee O(log N) height; without it, sorted inputs produce an O(N) degenerate skew.

name: QuickSort In-Place Means O(1) Auxiliary Space
description: Overlooking the recursive call stack space of O(log n) to O(n).
correction: While QuickSort modifies the array in-place, the recursion call stack requires O(log N) auxiliary space (or O(N) worst case).

name: Greedy Choice Always Yields Global Optimal for Knapsack
description: Assuming greedy density sorting works for 0/1 Knapsack just because it works for Fractional Knapsack.
correction: 0/1 Knapsack exhibits overlapping subproblems requiring Dynamic Programming because discrete item indivisibility breaks the greedy choice property.

name: Dijkstra Algorithm Handles Negative Weight Edges If No Negative Cycles
description: Believing Dijkstra's algorithm correctly calculates shortest paths with negative edges as long as there are no negative cycles.
correction: Dijkstra greedily marks nodes as visited assuming paths can only grow longer. Negative weights violate this monotonic assumption; Bellman-Ford must be used.

name: High Accuracy on Imbalanced Data Means Good Model Performance
description: Relying on raw accuracy when 99% of samples belong to the negative class.
correction: With severe class imbalance, a naive majority-class classifier achieves high accuracy while failing to detect the minority class. Precision, Recall, PR-AUC or F1-score are necessary.

name: Zero Training Error Implies Perfect Learning
description: Equating 100% training accuracy with superior intelligence rather than catastrophic overfitting.
correction: Zero training loss often indicates the model has memorized training noise and will fail to generalize to unseen test distributions.

name: High Feature Correlation Implies Causal Importance
description: Assuming strongly correlated features are root causes of the target variable.
correction: Correlation measures linear association, not directionality or confounding factors. Confounders can induce spurious correlations.

name: Adding More Layers Always Improves Representation
description: Assuming deeper neural networks unconditionally learn better without vanishing gradients or degradation problems.
correction: Without residual connections, normalization, and careful initialization, deeper networks suffer from gradient vanishing/exploding and optimization degradation.

name: Scaling Features Is Unnecessary for Distance-Based Algorithms
description: Applying KNN or SVM without normalizing numerical features of differing scales.
correction: Distance metrics (Euclidean) are dominated by features with large absolute ranges, effectively muting smaller-scale informative features unless standardized.

name: Fitting Scaler on Entire Dataset Before Train-Test Split
description: Standardizing the entire dataset before splitting, leading to data leakage.
correction: Fitting transformers/scalers on the full dataset leaks test set statistics (mean, variance) into training, artificially inflating evaluation metrics.
